title: His father's family out of slavery
summary: He tells how his grandmother carried his father north from Virginia and how his father educated himself in the Biddles' library.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And when he worked that, my old man was brilliant. He was brilliant. And he's just out of slavery.

When he left Virginia, his mother had one -- my uncle was born just in slavery. Just, he was about a year old. And my father was just born out of slavery, see. And she had these two kids, she had them, one, pullin' my uncle along, and she had my father over her shoulder and she didn't -- over her shoulder, and she didn't know even which way she was goin', even. But she followed the crowd and we got to Pennsylvania, to Philadelphia. She said she didn't know whether she was goin' up, north, or goin' west or east. So that's what my grandmother said, that everybody was making it up north, so she made it up north with them, see.

But, he had done a lot of studyin', and after he studied, he, then he went with the Biddles, I told you. And when he had time off, between meals or anything like that, he'd sit down and read those books. And, you know, they had a big library there because old Colonel Biddle was the head of the Pennsylvania National Guard, see. So he'd read those books, well, he'd come up with
You see, we tried to carry on, but in a poor way, we carried on.
